text:
maya: Quick heads up — I started a perf run on mixtral-8x with AWQ int8 + RoPE scale 0.75 and saw a clear latency/regression compared to the baseline. attaching short trace and repro steps.

devon: Can you paste the top-level numbers? p50/p95 and token/s?

maya: p50 went from ~35ms -> ~58ms, p95 92ms -> 160ms for single-stream inference. tokens/s dropped ~28%. CPU overhead increased on kernel selection path (more fallbacks).

alex: Do you have the profiler flamegraph? suspect fallback to generic matmul kernels after quant paths fail.

maya: Uploaded the trace to /perf/artifacts/183012 — flame shows heavy time in matmul_gemm_generic and in kv_cache::rehash.

infra-bot: perf-job #183012 started: bench.mixtral.awq-int8.rope075 (run id 202) — logs: https://ci.internal/reports/183012

samir: Quick thought — AWQ calibration might be shifting scales for qkv causing larger intermediate magnitudes, triggers different kernel choices (fallback to fp32 path). Did you run AWQ with the recommended calibration prompts?

maya: I used the default small prompt set. Re-ran with expanded calibrator (50 diverse prompts) — numbers improved but still ~15% worse than baseline. Accuracy delta: AWQ int8 shows ~0.9% soft-token perplexity increase vs FP16 baseline; GPTQ int8 on same model shows ~0.25% increase.

julia: That suggests quant noise is tolerable but kernel path changes are the bigger cost. If matmul kernel selector sees int8 layout mismatch it can route to slower code. Can you dump kernel decisions?

maya: Dumped per-layer kernel decisions: many early layers used int8-gemm-optimized but layers 9,10,11 switched to generic_gemm (non-optimized) — those correspond to layers with larger RoPE scaling factors.

devon: RoPE scaling interaction: scaling increases magnitude of rotary embeddings, which may increase Q/K variance; AWQ's per-channel scales could be hitting clipping thresholds. We should test: (1) run AWQ calib but clamp scales; (2) try per-tensor calibration; (3) try GPTQ on just the problematic layers.

alex: Also check KV cache layout — if head/kv dims are non-contiguous after quant, our KV caching code does a reshape that forces a memcopy and drops into slower path. That explains the kv_cache::rehash hotspot.

maya: Reproduced memcopy: when head_dim % 8 != 0 after quant reorder we fall back. mixtral-8x head_dim is 64 but AWQ packing changed stride.

samir: Two quick experiments I ran locally: (A) AWQ int8 with calibration prompts = 50, clamp scales to 0.02..0.98 => p50 improved 10% (still +8% vs baseline) and no kernel fallback on layers 1-8. (B) Hybrid: AWQ on most layers + GPTQ on 9..11 => p50 almost baseline (+1-2%). Accuracy delta for hybrid ~0.35%.

julia: Good. Actionable items: add a kernel-selector guard that prefers int8-optimized kernels even if scale variance high (but validate correctness), and add a fallback policy to try GPTQ on layers that trigger generic_gemm. Also add KV packing check in the runtime to avoid memcopies when possible.

paul: For batching heuristics: did anyone try changing batch/continuous-batching thresholds? The regression might be worse for single-stream; with micro-batching we could amortize kernel overhead.

maya: Yes — increasing batch window to 8 reduced p50 by ~12% in the AWQ case (amortizes the extra kernel cost) but increases p95 for single user. Tradeoff obvious.

devon: Proposed short checklist: 
- Re-run AWQ calib with expanded prompts + clamp (maya)
- Profile per-layer kernel decisions and publish mapping (maya + alex)
- Try hybrid AWQ/GPTQ per-layer strategy on mixtral-8x (samir)
- Add KV packing guard to runtime and measure memcpy elimination (eng-runtime small PR) (julia)
- Evaluate FP8 on top 2 attention layers to see accuracy vs perf (paul)

alex: For reproducibility, here's the repro command I used: 
```
./tools/bench_infer.py --model mixtral-8x --mode single-stream --quant awq-int8 --rope-scale 0.75 --calib-set=calib/50-prompts.txt --batch-window=1 --profile=flame
```

maya: And the quick kernel-dump helper: 
```
TRACE_KERNELS=1 ./bin/runtime --model mixtral-8x --quant awq-int8 --run-profile
cat /tmp/kernel_dump.json | jq '.layers[] | {layer, kernel}'
```

samir: I'll open a draft RFC for per-layer hybrid quant strategy and add a simple selection script to try AWQ vs GPTQ per-layer based on a tiny 100-prompt eval.

julia: I'll take the memcpy/kv packing ticket. If we can avoid memcopy for the 8-aligned case we likely recover most of the perf.

maya: I'll push the expanded calib set and results to the artifact bucket and tag the perf-job. ping @devon @alex when I have the new traces. :slightly_smiling_face:

devon: Thanks — quick wins look like: clamp calib scales + hybrid GPTQ on 9-11 + KV packing fix. If those land we should be under 5% regression.

infra-bot: perf-job #183012 completed: baseline vs awq-int8.rope075 report at https://ci.internal/reports/183012/summary — summary artifact: s3://perf-reports/183012/summary.json

maya: OK closing this thread for now, reopening if new traces show other hotspots.
